control.outcome: First main query OOM137 at2GiB; no unchanged repeat.

singleVariable: Change only the instance query-planning-budget threshold from100 to1, leaving the D source/negation/retirement/aggregate profile unchanged. This selects the planner algorithm earlier; it is not a memory ceiling.

sources.mechanism: For each connected component, compare the connected-subgraph count against the threshold; use greedy planning above it, dynamic programming otherwise.
Stop counting once the threshold is exceeded. For threshold1, any component with more than one counted subgraph selects greedy. Threshold0 selects greedy for every nonempty component.
The parameter is size_t and its source default is1500; this project explicitly pins100.
The constructor registers the setting without a setting-specific constraint; the positive constraints shown apply to timeout and scan threads.

Its parser uses std::stoull and converts to size_t. On the observed64bit Linux target, the representable unsigned range is0 through18446744073709551615; the experiment uses plain decimal1, avoiding zero/overflow/parser edge cases.

evidenceAndInference.observed: The failed D query already emitted241 greedy-planner messages at threshold100 before its cgroup OOM. Lowering the threshold cannot change those already-greedy components.
evidenceAndInference.hypothesis: Smaller still-dynamic subplans and their candidate combinations may account for remaining memory. A threshold1 can change those selections. Existing logs do not identify every subplan or an allocation stack, so improvement remains uncertain.
evidenceAndInference.notClaimed: Neither threshold100 nor1 imposes a native memory bound or proves that greedy planning itself cannot OOM.

executionPolicy.cleanup: Restore100 and read it back in finally. If the engine OOMs, retain UNKNOWN reservation and forensic ACK/data state; same-CID recovery restores/readbacks100 before resident refresh.
